The skill depends on public network lookups for current documentation and pricing, so stale data and network access should be disclosed.

remediation.suggestion: Keep the stale-data warning and document the exact Microsoft endpoints the skill may request.

content.user_title: Recommend Azure VM and VMSS Options
content.value_statement: Choosing Azure VM sizes can be slow and expensive to research. This skill compares workload needs, VM families, VMSS guidance, and public pricing data.
actual_capabilities: Matches workloads to Azure VM families using the included reference guide.
Recommends single VM or VMSS based on scaling, availability, and instance count.
Uses Azure Retail Prices API patterns for consumption, reservation, and currency estimates.
Guides verification with current Microsoft Learn documentation before final recommendations.
Explains trade-offs across cost, CPU, memory, GPU, storage, HPC, and confidential computing.
limitations: Does not deploy, modify, or inspect Azure resources.
Reference data may become stale unless live documentation is verified.
Pricing estimates exclude full networking, storage, licensing, quota, and private discount context.
Availability and regional support must be confirmed for each subscription and workload.

use_cases.title: Plan a scalable web tier
use_cases.description: Compare single VM and VMSS options for stateless services that need autoscale and load balancing.

use_cases.title: Choose database infrastructure
use_cases.description: Select memory, storage, and availability options for relational databases, caches, and large data workloads.

use_cases.title: Estimate compute budget ranges
use_cases.description: Compare hourly and monthly VM costs across regions, pricing types, and expected instance counts.

prompt_templates.title: Recommend a basic VM
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend an Azure VM for a small Linux web app in eastus. Balance cost and performance, and explain the main trade-off.

prompt_templates.title: Compare VM families
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Azure VM families for a PostgreSQL workload needing 8 vCPUs, high memory, premium SSD, and predictable performance.

prompt_templates.title: Design a VMSS option
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a VMSS design for a stateless API with two minimum instances, CPU autoscale, zone resilience, and monthly cost estimates.

prompt_templates.title: Build a constrained shortlist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create three Azure compute options for ML inference with GPU needs, Spot tolerance, Linux, westus3 pricing, and failover considerations.

output_examples.input: I need a low-cost VM for a development web server in eastus.
output: Primary recommendation: B-series for burstable, low-cost development workloads.
Alternative: D-series if sustained CPU performance matters more than price.
Next step: verify current regional availability and retail pricing before purchase.

output_examples.input: Should I use VMSS for a public API that has daily traffic spikes?
output: Recommendation: VMSS Flexible with at least two instances for production availability.
Autoscale plan: schedule a higher baseline before traffic spikes and add CPU-based scale-out.
Cost note: estimate both minimum and maximum instance counts because VMSS charges per VM.

output_examples.input: Compare options for a memory-heavy database workload.
output: Primary family: E-series for high memory per vCPU and predictable database performance.
Large-memory option: M-series when the workload needs very high RAM capacity.
Trade-off: memory-optimized sizes cost more than balanced D-series instances.

best_practices: Provide workload type, region, operating system, performance needs, and budget priority.
Verify current Microsoft Learn specifications before acting on a recommendation.
Estimate VMSS costs at minimum, average, and maximum instance counts.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill to deploy or change Azure resources.
Do not rely on stale reference data for final production decisions.
Do not request price estimates without region, operating system, and SKU assumptions.

faq.question: Does this skill require an Azure account?
faq.answer: No. It uses public Microsoft documentation and the unauthenticated Azure Retail Prices API.

faq.question: Can it deploy virtual machines or scale sets?
faq.answer: No. It only recommends options and explains trade-offs for planning decisions.

faq.question: Does it support VM Scale Sets?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps decide when VMSS is appropriate and suggests orchestration, autoscale, and load balancing patterns.

faq.question: Are the pricing estimates final quotes?
faq.answer: No. They are retail estimates and may exclude discounts, licensing, storage, networking, and taxes.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it compare GPU, HPC, and confidential computing sizes?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes family guidance, but current availability and specifications should be verified.
